text:
GitHub Copilot just made model choice a dial, not a default.

What changed: Copilot rolled out selectable model tiers -- efficiency, balance, intelligence -- instead of one auto-picked model for every request.

What it actually does: it lets you match the model to the job. A quick one-line edit doesn't need the same reasoning horsepower as a hard refactor across a whole service, and now you can choose that on purpose instead of defaulting to the biggest model every time.

Why builders should care: speed and cost stop being accidents of whichever model happened to answer. You start spending your heaviest reasoning budget on your hardest problems, and your fastest, cheapest tier on the busywork.

Try this this week: take your next two tasks -- one small fix, one real rebuild -- and deliberately run them on different tiers. Notice where the cheaper tier is plenty, and where it clearly is not.

The bigger signal: for a while the only AI skill anyone talked about was prompting. Now which model you reach for, and when, is its own literacy.

Save this for your AI stack.
